thread.title_full: Michael Jordan's NASCAR lawyer pulls off another huge win in landmark case - NewsBreak

author: Rory Robinson
title: Michael Jordan's NASCAR lawyer pulls off another huge win in landmark case - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
3 hours ago
Michael Jordan is known as a serial winner and, on most lists, as the greatest NBA player ever, so it's no surprise that those around him share his pursuit of greatness.
Jordan's NASCAR lawyer, Jeffrey Kessler, has also made a career out of racking up wins and settlements in court. Kessler was a major catalyst in the 23XI Racing frontman's historic settlement in a long, fought-out antitrust lawsuit against the sport that lasted 435 days.
A federal jury in Manhattan found Live Nation Entertainment and Ticketmaster guilty of operating as an illegal anticompetitive monopoly, which excited DC Attorney General Brian Schwalb. Jordan has remained visible throughout the Cup season following weeks of success after Kessler's help.
The jury found that the companies held monopoly power in major ticketing markets, suppressing competition and overcharging consumers by $1.72 per ticket across 22 states, totaling hundreds of millions of dollars.
The case revealed damaging internal communications, with employees calling customers "so stupid" and joking about "robbing them blind." These findings weren't in the company's favor, reinforcing claims of exploitation.
Kessler served as lead outside counsel for a coalition of 34 states and the District of Columbia. "It is time to hold them accountable," he said when taking the case.
Kessler described Live Nation as a "monopolistic bully" during the proceedings. His work with Jordan and 23XI Racing secured permanent charters for the team and unlocked increased revenue streams, setting the stage for a dominant 2026 season.
23XI Racing has backed up that stability with results after No. 45 Toyota Camry driver Tyler Reddick opened the Cup Series season by winning four of the first six races. Bubba Wallace has also maintained consistent finishes and jumped into 8th in the Driver standings following an 11th-place finish at Bristol.
Kessler helped Jordan and 23XI Racing earn permanent charter status The implications of the Ticketmaster verdict are just beginning, as the case now enters a remedies phase under U.S. District Judge Arun Subramanian. Possible consequences of the ruling might involve breaking up Live Nation and Ticketmaster, dividing their assets, and imposing financial penalties.
Live Nation has already expressed its intent to fight the ruling. Its legal team argues that the company's dominance stems from "excellence and effort" rather than illegal conduct.
Kessler works as a lawyer at the global firm Winston & Strawn, which earned a historic $1.369 billion in revenue last year. His work has been featured in high-profile cases, including successfully representing Tom Brady in Deflategate and a lawsuit that helped the U.S. Women's National Soccer Team secure equal pay.
